hypotheses.justification: The statement only uses `μ.prod ν`, and `Measure.prod` takes no instance arguments. In Mathlib (Measure/Prod.lean, line 172) it is defined as `if SFinite ν then bind μ (fun x => map (Prod.mk x) ν) else 0`, so the junk value is `0` when `ν` is not s-finite. Without the hypothesis, the proof splits on `SFinite ν`. If `ν` is s-finite, run the current argument with `haveI`. If it is not, `μ.prod ν = 0`, so `μ.prod ν (s \ G) = 0` holds by unfolding `Measure.prod` with `if_neg`, i.e. `simp [Measure.prod, h]`. The theorem therefore stays true and provable without `[SFinite ν]`.
